newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sen. Lott - staff identifying tax differences.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sen. Lott - staff identifying tax differences.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Monday staff worked over the weekend to identify areas of agreement and disagreement on the tax bill, but that no one was yet at the "point of giving."

"I don't think anybody is at the point of giving, I think everybody's identifying where are there no differences, where can we easily agree, where (are) the zones where we probably can work it out pretty quickly," the Mississippi Republican told reporters. "And then there will be the ones that are of ultimate importance, either to us or the administration, and we'll have to work through that," he added.

Lott is one of the House-Senate lawmakers trying to put together a final tax bill from the separate versions passed by each chamber. They hope to pass a final tax bill and send it to President Clinton before the August recess.
Lott said he will be among Republican and Democratic lawmakers to meet with Clinton Tuesday.

"I think probably we will just talk in general terms about what we hope to achieve and it may not be all on tax and budget. It may be on NATO enlargement and Bosnia," Lott said, adding that he has not been informed about the agenda for the meeting.

Asked whether the Senate could agree to some type of corporate alternative minimum tax (AMT) relief, Lott replied: "It's possible, but I haven't really started looking for the middle ground there yet. But I think there is a possibility at some point that could be achieved."
Progress was made on the balanced budget.
"The balanced budget side has made real good progress," he told reporters.

On proposals to raise the age of Medicare eligibility, Lott said: "It looks like the administration will have concerns about that, as well as some Democrats in the House, but we're still talking about that.
"In the end, we'll have to make all those decisions sort of in a block, some decisions like that will work up to sort of the managment level and there will be give and take."

Asked whether on Medicare the likely final trade-off would be no eligibility age increase, but some income-testing, Lott replied: "I wouldn't be prepared to give up on any of those yet. I think they're the right thing to do."
